sections.title: Front matter
sections.extract: arXiv:1511.00400v2 [math.GT] 26 May 2016 Reidemeister torsion, hyperbolic three-manifolds, and character varieties Joan Porti∗ November 6, 2018 Abstract This is a survey on Reidemeister torsion for hyperbolic three-manifolds of ﬁnite volume. Torsions are viewed as topological invariants and also as functions on the variety of representations in SL2(C). In both cases, the torsions may also be computed after composing

sections.title: Introduction
sections.extract: []{#sec:intro label="sec:intro"} The goal of this paper is to survey some results on Reidemeister torsions of orientable, hyperbolic three-manifolds of finite volume. Torsions are viewed as invariants of hyperbolic manifolds and also as functions on the variety of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-characters. The paper uses combinatorial torsion, though some relevant developments described here are proved using analytic

sections.title: Combinatorial and analytic torsions
sections.extract: []{#sec:combandanl label="sec:combandanl"} This section overviews the definition and main properties of combinatorial torsion, as they are used later in some proofs. It also recalls briefly the definition of analytic torsion, as it is used in many relevant results.

sections.title: Geometric properties of combinatorial torsion
sections.extract: This subsection recalls the basic properties of combinatorial torsion, the main one being Mayer-Vietoris, useful for cut and paste. Bundles over $S^1$ are also considered, in particular instead of just the torsion it is more convenient to consider the twisted Alexander polynomial, which is a torsion by [@Kitano96]. The subsection finishes with examples.

sections.title: Appendix A Not approximating the trivial representation
sections.extract: []{#sec:notapprox label="sec:notapprox"} For a manifold $M^3$ there are components of $X(M^3,\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}))$ that consist of characters of abelian representations. When $b_1(M^3)=1$ those components are curves, and their union is denoted by $$X^{ab}(M^3,\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C})).$$ The number of components of $X^{ab}(M^3,\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{C}))$ depends on the torsion of $H_1(M^3;\mathbb{Z})$.
